case_title: Bhaikon @ Bakul Borah v. State of Assam
weapon: Sharp cutting weapon caused chin and mandible cut injuries; death by throttling (weapon used for throttling not identified). A 'dao' was seized from the farm house.
evidence_type: Eyewitness; corroborative witness testimony (father, brothers, co-villagers); medical (post-mortem); recovery (seized underwear, bed sheet, dao)
aggravating_circumstances: Rape and murder; body dumped in a place surrounded by bushes and shrubs
mitigating_circumstances: Youth of the accused (age 33), noted by the High Court
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302 and 376 IPC; death for s.302; RI for life for s.376 with fine of Rs. 10,000
high_court_outcome: Conviction confirmed; death sentence altered to life imprisonment (fine Rs. 1,000); s.376 sentence reduced to 7 years
neutral_facts: On a day in late March 2000, around noon, the victim, a 22-year-old woman, went to a field near an embankment to attend her goats. When she did not return, her father searched for her. While searching, he heard loud laughter from a farm house belonging to the accused. Later he found the victim's body lying on the embankment path with a cut injury on her chin and blood oozing from her body. The victim's brother and other villagers gathered at the scene, and the accused came and enquired. Police seized the victim's underwear, which was stained with semen. Later they seized the accused's blue underwear, a bed sheet, a sporting item and a dao from the farm house. An eyewitness who was working at the farm house stated that he saw the accused and a companion follow the victim, saw them behave indecently and commit rape, and saw the accused throttle her. The two then dragged the body into a spot surrounded by shrubs and bushes. The post-mortem found a cut injury on the chin, bruises on the neck, a fractured trachea and death from asphyxia due to throttling. The medical examiner found no spermatozoa on a vaginal smear and no injury on the genital organs. Statements of the victim's family and co-villagers who saw the body were recorded.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to throttling; cut injury over lower chin with cut mandible; bruises on neck; fractured trachea
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of PW-1; corroborative evidence of PW-2 (father); medical evidence of PW-9 (post-mortem); evidence of PWs 3, 4, 7 and 8 and co-villagers' statements
witness_credibility: PW-1 held an independent and reliable eyewitness; his silence explained by fear of the khukri; the trial court found him trustworthy. PW-2 and PW-9 found consistent with prosecution story.
post_offence_conduct: Accused came to the scene after the body was found and enquired; according to the eyewitness, he returned home after the incident
trial_duration: offence: 29.03.2000; trial judgment: 18.03.2006; High Court: 26.09.2006; Supreme Court: 03.05.2013
legal_representation: Accused: Pandit Parmanand Katara (senior counsel), with Abhishek Sharma, C.K. Sucharita and Kusum Lata Sharma. State: Navnit Kumar, Avijit Roy, Corporate Law Group.
investigation_status: FIR registered (GD Entry No. 389); charge-sheet filed; trial completed in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted; death for s.302 and life for s.376. High Court: conviction upheld; death altered to life imprisonment; s.376 sentence reduced to 7 years. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Eyewitness PW-1 is reliable and corroborated by PW-2 and PW-9; no automatic release after 14 years on commutation of death sentence.
defence_argument: Eyewitness PW-1 unreliable; no mark of sexual violence on genital organs so s.376 conviction unsustainable; accused should have been released after 14 years since death sentence was commuted.
legal_principle_applied: Life imprisonment means imprisonment for whole of life subject to remission under Articles 72 and 161; remission on commutation to be exercised cautiously considering gravity; eyewitness and medical evidence assessed as corroborative.
precedent_relied_upon: Life Convict @ Khoka Prasanta Sen v. B.K. Srivastava (2013) 3 SCC 425; Mohinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2013) 3 SCC 294; Sangeet v. State of Haryana (2013) 2 SCC 452; Rameshbhai Chandubhai Rathod (2) v. State of Gujarat (2011) 2 SCC 764; Chhote Lal v. State of MP (2011) 8 SCR 239; Mulla v. State of UP (2010) 3 SCC 508; Maru Ram v. Union of India (1981) 1 SCC 107; State of MP v. Ratan Singh (1976) 3 SCC 470; Gopal Vinayak Godse v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1961 SC 600; Swami Shraddananda (2) v. State of Karnataka (2008) 13 SCC 767; Sahib Hussain v. State of Rajasthan 2013 (6) Scale 219
sentencing_rationale: Life imprisonment is for the whole of life subject to executive remission; where death is commuted, remission must be exercised cautiously considering gravity; no automatic release after 14 years.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Youth of the accused (age 33), taken note of by the High Court in declining the death sentence
judicial_aggravating_factors: Heinous nature of rape and murder; disposal of body in a place surrounded by bushes and shrubs; gravity of offence relevant to executive remission
